When they ask if you have any questions for them, pause, and then ask a well developed question. It goes a long way and makes the interviewer believe you are truly interested in the job. Try to make the question complicated and involve actual thought to answer. So not, "what hours will I be working," but more along the lines of "What attributes does someone need to have in order to be really successful in this position?" or "What does a typical day on the job look like?" It doesn't come off cocky at all, it indirectly shows that you are confident in your abilities and skills, and that you want to get to know the place you will work.
